cast/4 allowlists vs mass assignment             ALREADY-GOOD       explicit field lists; server-managed fields non-castable
validations (UX) vs DB constraints (truth)       1 FINDING + clean   surface_config unmapped unique index; 30+ schemas mapped
embedded schemas for JSONB content               REJECTED-W-REASON  deliberate raw-map (headless CMS), validated by schema-v2

encrypted_map.ex / encrypted_binary.ex           ALREADY-GOOD       Cloak AES-GCM, raises on decrypt failure = fail-closed

content.value: NAMED FAILURE MODE: DELETE /v1/auth/webauthn/credentials/:id (router.ex:1227, pipe_through [:user_auth,:require_user]) passes the raw :id path param unmodified through webauthn_controller.ex:188-189 into Barkpark.Accounts.Webauthn.delete_credential/2, which calls Repo.get_by(WebauthnCredential, id: id, user_id: uid). WebauthnCredential PK is :binary_id. Any authenticated user hitting DELETE .../credentials/garbage (non-UUID :id) makes Ecto cast 'garbage' to :binary_id inside get_by -> Ecto.CastError -> HTTP 500, instead of the intended 404 not_found. The user_id: uid scoping does NOT save it — the cast on id: fires regardless. This is the exact binary_id CastError scar class; the canonical guard Barkpark.Repo.uuid_or_nil/1 is not on this path.
Filed: task-b5af6673bfb773ea. Protective test (fails before fix): authenticated DELETE with a non-UUID :id returns 404, not 500.

blocks.text: Finding 2 (priority 2) — search_surface_config: unmapped unique index -> ConstraintError 500 on concurrent first PUT

content.value: NAMED FAILURE MODE (validations-vs-constraints, FAILURE-B): migration 20260527100000:17-18 creates UNIQUE index search_surface_config_surface_scope_idx on (surface, scope). But SurfaceConfig.changeset/2 (surface_config.ex:36) casts only the 4 config fields and maps NO unique_constraint, and surface_configs.ex:136-140 does Repo.get_by then, on nil, Repo.insert() with NO on_conflict. External entry: search_controller.ex:270 and v1/media_controller.ex:156. Trigger: for a (surface,scope) with no row yet (a new dataset's first search-config PUT), two concurrent PUTs both see get_by=nil, both insert, the second violates the unique index -> Ecto.ConstraintError uncaught -> HTTP 500 instead of a clean update/idempotent upsert. Admin-gated and race-only (pre-seeded documents/media production rows unaffected), but the index exists and the changeset ignores it — the exact 'constraints are truth' gap.

content.value: Filed: task-1a4e660c18bb3046. Protective test (fails before fix): two inserts for the same new (surface,scope) — the second returns {:error, changeset} or is idempotent, not an uncaught ConstraintError.

blocks.text: Already-good (verified, no change) — the doctrine is largely held

content.value: binary_id scar, the other ~155 sites: SAFE via one of three guards — (a) canonical Repo.uuid_or_nil/1 at the context boundary (tenancy.ex 149/320/600, access.ex 127/404, auth.ex 214, status.ex 133, sharing/links.ex 97, bulldocs/events.ex 66/110, search/synonyms.ex 67, tickets/keys.ex, studio_chat.ex 62); (b) the doc_id->Document text-column indirection — the entire task-mutation surface (fence/mutations/release/close/move + content/writer/lifecycle) resolves the external doc_id string via find_task_by_doc_id (a query on the TEXT doc_id column) and passes only the fetched row's real UUID .id downward, so a garbage id returns 404 at the controller and never reaches a :binary_id query; (c) not a binary_id key (github conflict + webhook MutationEvent are integer keys validated by Integer.parse; onixedit staleness + task board query the :string doc_id field), or the id is DB-sourced (Oban job args, loaded rows).

cast/4 allowlists: every changeset uses an explicit field allowlist — zero __schema__(:fields)/Map.keys mass-assignment. Privilege/server-managed fields are deliberately excluded: User.failed_login_count/locked_until ('NEVER castable'), Webhook auto-disable + secret-rotation fields, and Membership.role is validated by inclusion against valid_roles with the role passed explicitly by callers. Access.Grant fails closed on its capability vocabulary (read/write/admin only).

Constraint parity: 30+ external-write schemas carry the DB constraint AND a matching changeset mapping, with every explicit name: verified byte-aligned to its migration index name (no vacuous mappings). users.email correctly pairs unsafe_validate_unique (UX) with unique_constraint + a real UNIQUE(email) (truth). No FAILURE-A (vacuous constraint) anywhere. plugin_settings/secrets have unmapped PK uniqueness but resolve the race in-DB via Repo.insert_or_update(on_conflict:), so they are SAFE — this is the pattern surface_config should copy. webhooks FKs are unmapped but tenant scope is server-resolved (client scope keys stripped), not external-reachable today.

Fail-closed modules: redaction.ex is an allowlist secret-log scrubber used ONLY by plugin Inspect impls that destructure specific fields first, so the struct-passthrough branch never receives a secret-bearing struct — appropriate, not leaky (and it is distinct from Envelope field-visibility redaction). encrypted_map.ex / encrypted_binary.ex are Cloak AES-GCM types that raise on decrypt failure = fail-closed. Embedded-schema-for-JSONB is deliberately rejected: Document.content is a raw map by design (one content model, many surfaces), validated by the schema-v2 validation layer, not Ecto embeds.

Watch-item (NOT filed — no live failure mode, would be speculative): Accounts.get_user/1 (accounts.ex:40) does an unguarded Repo.get(User, id). All current callers feed DB-sourced or already-cast UUIDs, so it is SAFE today; it becomes a 500 the instant any controller wires a raw :user_id/:id path param straight into it. One-line uuid_or_nil guard would pre-empt that, but per the improvement doctrine there is no named failure mode today, so it stays a note.

No FAILURE-A (vacuous constraint) anywhere. plugin_settings/secrets have unmapped PK uniqueness but resolve the race in-DB via Repo.insert_or_update(on_conflict:), so they are SAFE — this is the pattern surface_config should copy. webhooks FKs are unmapped but tenant scope is server-resolved (client scope keys stripped), not external-reachable today.

Fail-closed modules: redaction.ex is an allowlist secret-log scrubber used ONLY by plugin Inspect impls that destructure specific fields first, so the struct-passthrough branch never receives a secret-bearing struct — appropriate, not leaky (and it is distinct from Envelope field-visibility redaction). encrypted_map.ex / encrypted_binary.ex are Cloak AES-GCM types that raise on decrypt failure = fail-closed. Embedded-schema-for-JSONB is deliberately rejected: Document.content is a raw map by design (one content model, many surfaces), validated by the schema-v2 validation layer, not Ecto embeds.

Watch-item (NOT filed — no live failure mode, would be speculative): Accounts.get_user/1 (accounts.ex:40) does an unguarded Repo.get(User, id). All current callers feed DB-sourced or already-cast UUIDs, so it is SAFE today; it becomes a 500 the instant any controller wires a raw :user_id/:id path param straight into it. One-line uuid_or_nil guard would pre-empt that, but per the improvement doctrine there is no named failure mode today, so it stays a note.
